data.goal: Make every batch F-7 publishes durable (Room row + per-batch files under ~/.rectify) and surface it as the third, desktop-only segment of RectifyWindow's inspector tab strip: a LazyColumn of Today/Yesterday/Older-grouped rows with a union-bbox thumbnail, title, meta line and status chip, plus an In-progress badge and a 'claude · session <id>' footer — without a new Gradle module, a new design-system component, or any change to F-7's merged wire contract.
data.problemStatement: PER-2 (QA tester) has no durable record of batches already sent to the coding agent. FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.publish prunes every handoff-slot directory except the newest and data-handoff-api states verbatim 'No history, no ring buffer, no expiry', so the previous send's images vanish on the next send and nothing at all survives an app restart. There is therefore no way to see what has already been reported and in what state without re-testing, and F-9's Verify loop has no durable original frame to diff against.
data.highLevelDescription: One persistence vertical hung off the existing mirror surface. Write path: MirrorViewModel.resolveAndSend() already holds `frozen`, `held.bitmap`, `held.bytes` and, after assembly, `(envelope, images)` as in-memory locals; inside the SAME withContext(Dispatchers.Default) assembly block it additionally encodes one small thumbnail PNG from the union bounding box of the batch's annotation rects. On `published.onSuccess`, BEFORE postSideEffect(SendComplete), the VM calls `recordSentBatch(...): Result<Unit>` and consumes it with `.onFailure { log.w }` and nothing else — the persist lives in its own failure domain and can never touch SendPhase. Down the stack RecordSentBatchUseCaseImpl → HistoryRepositoryImpl writes bulk bytes through a `fun interface BatchFileStore` (desktop java.io, null-returning stand-in elsewhere, never throws) to ~/.rectify/history/<sanitised batchId>/{frame.png, crop-N.png, hierarchy.xml}, then inserts the parent row plus normalised history_annotation children in one @Transaction with whatever paths the store returned (or null). Read path: HistoryEntryDao exposes Flow<List<HistoryEntryEntity>> ordered sentAtMs DESC → HistoryEntryMapper.toModel → ObserveHistoryUseCase (bare Flow) → collected once in MirrorViewModel's container init into MirrorUiState.history, which feeds both the list and the badge. Render path: MirrorHistoryTab = Column { LazyColumn(weight(1f)) { group headers + HistoryRow items }; footer }, grouping computed at render time by pure groupHistory(entries, nowMs, zone); the thumbnail is a few-KB BLOB decoded with the already-used ByteArray.decodeToImageBitmap(), so the list performs zero filesystem reads. Two edits in RectifyWindow.kt close the loop.
data.background: F-7 (resolve-and-send-mcp) is merged and ships AnnotationHandoff/AnnotationEnvelope, mintSessionId, EnvelopeAssembly and CropEncoder. ShellTab.History, the Cmd+3 shortcut, SidebarTabs' per-tab count, HistoryRow, StatusPill/StatusPillTone and AppButtonSize.ListAction are all already built and registered — only the panel body (`else -> Unit` in RectifyWindow.kt) and all persistence are missing. data-database-impl is a live but never-instantiated Room skeleton: AppDatabase is a lazy Koin single nothing injects, and neither ~/rectify.db nor ~/.rectify/ exists on disk, which is what makes relocating the DB and staying at @Database(version = 1) safe and makes Step 0 a blocking spike.

assumptions: AS-1: a single integration point (the resolveAndSend call site) is sufficient to trigger the persist; F-8 never polls or reads back the handoff slot.
AS-2: AC-22's 'title/summary' is the batch's first annotation's comment text — no separate generated summary field.
AS-3: the static 'claude' agent label is acceptable; mcp-application ships exactly one tool and one consumer.
AS-4: Sent shares Verified's neutral (StatusPillTone.Neutral / ink3) tone until product says otherwise.
AS-29: BatchFileStore never throws and returns null on any failure; Android/iOS bind a null-returning stand-in, unreachable in practice because UnsupportedAnnotationHandoff.publish throws first.
AS-30: assembly, crop encoding and the thumbnail encode all run inside the existing withContext(Dispatchers.Default) boundaries already documented in resolveAndSend's KDoc.

PLAN-AS-1 (resolved plan-stage question): core/payload/CropWindow.kt#cropWindow uses designPad=14f, boxW=84f, boxH=72f and returns a render window (srcOffset/srcSize/dstSize/scale), not PNG bytes. It is NOT reused for the thumbnail. FR-29's pad=18 / bw=bh=40 is the prototype's crop() formula; the plan reimplements it as a pure thumbnailRect(union, frameSize, designPad = 18f, designWidth = 296f) in core/history/, keeping cropWindow's design-space pad-scaling convention (pad = designPad * frameWidth / designWidth).

PLAN-AS-2 (resolved plan-stage question): the repo contains zero pluralStringResource usages and zero <plurals> resources. The note count ships as two plain keys (mirror_history_meta_note_one / mirror_history_meta_note_other) selected by a pure function; no 's' is hand-concatenated and no plural API is introduced.

PLAN-AS-3 (resolved plan-stage question): SidebarTabs' rendering of a zero count is not relied on at all — tabCounts is built with buildMap and the ShellTab.History key is omitted when the In-progress count is 0, which makes AC-34 true regardless of SidebarTabs' behaviour.

PLAN-AS-4: HistoryRow ships a 56dp thumbnail plate (registry: components.json#history-row) while the design quotes 44×44. The shipped component is reused as-is; the encoded thumbnail is capped at 128px on its longest edge so it stays crisp inside the 56dp plate. Changing the plate size is a design-system change no AC requires.

PLAN-AS-5: Room's builder() does not touch the filesystem — the database file is opened on first query — so a bad path or unwritable home surfaces as a query exception inside the guarded Flow or inside resultLauncher, not as a crash while Koin constructs the graph.
PLAN-AS-6: the batch directory name is batchId.replace(Regex("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"), "_") because mintSessionId embeds a device id that is not guaranteed filesystem-safe.
PLAN-AS-7: the row's id is the envelope's sessionId; a same-millisecond collision on the same device+frame degrades to an overwrite via @Insert(onConflict = REPLACE) rather than a crash.

constraints.text: Desktop-only (jvm target) — matches F-7's desktop-only AnnotationHandoff and RectifyWindow, the only host for the tab strip.

Must use the existing Room KMP scaffold (data-database-api/data-database-impl); F-8 is its first real consumer. KSP is already configured for kspAndroid/kspIosArm64/kspIosSimulatorArm64/kspDesktop — do not re-wire it.
Must ingest exclusively via the existing AnnotationHandoff/AnnotationEnvelope contract; AnnotationEnvelope's field order is wire-breaking and is not touched.
DB relocates to ~/.rectify/rectify.db AND stays at @Database(version = 1) with no Migration — the two decisions ship together or not at all. Destructive migration is disabled repo-wide.
No new Gradle module: MirrorHost's KDoc states there is exactly one call site, and a :presentation-feature-history module would force a second koinViewModel().
No new runtime dependency: no okio, no kotlinx-io, no image library. kotlinx-datetime is already in the version catalog (one build-file line, not a new dependency).

:compose-application has NO test wiring — nothing testable may land there. Pure logic lives in presentation-feature-mirror/core/history/ (commonTest), data-repository-impl (commonTest) or data-database-impl (desktopTest).
commonTest compiles for iOS: backtick test names containing a comma or a colon fail compileTestKotlinIosArm64. Plain camelCase names only (apostrophes are verified fine).
NFR-4: no network egress — all batch storage is local filesystem plus the local database; no analytics, no telemetry, no crash-report payloads carrying annotation text.
Step 0 is a blocking spike. Room has never been instantiated in this repo; no entity/DAO/repository work starts until an insert+observe round-trip is green on desktop.

risks.text: Room's KMP toolchain (KSP output, generated AppDatabaseConstructor actuals, BundledSQLiteDriver linkage and packaging, schemas/ export) has literally never been exercised in this repo; the first real table may surface build or packaging problems unrelated to F-8's logic.
risks.mitigation: Step 0 blocking spike, timeboxed to half a day, landed as data-database-impl/src/desktopTest/.../HistoryEntryDaoTest.kt so the proof is committed rather than thrown away. If the bundled driver fights desktop packaging, that is a scope conversation, not an in-branch debug session.

risks.text: Staying at schema version 1 while changing the entity set would crash any machine that somehow already holds a v1 rectify.db.
risks.mitigation: Relocating the file to ~/.rectify/rectify.db in the same change makes a pre-existing file impossible by construction. The two decisions ship together; if the relocation is dropped, the version bump plus a Migration becomes mandatory.

risks.text: A full-resolution union-bbox crop would be hundreds of KB per row, contradicting the 'few KB BLOB' basis of the thumbnail decision and ballooning MirrorUiState at scale.
risks.mitigation: Downscale before encoding: crop+scale the union window to <=128px on its longest edge into a scratch ImageBitmap (commonMain Canvas(ImageBitmap) + drawImageRect) and hand THAT to the existing CropEncoder. Keeps one encoder seam. Fallback if the common Canvas path misbehaves off the main thread: do the scale inside a desktop AwtCropEncoder sibling (getSubimage + getScaledInstance) bound by qualifier.

risks.text: Adding two non-defaulted MirrorViewModel constructor params breaks every existing VM test until MirrorFakes is updated.
risks.mitigation: Update MirrorFakes.kt in the same commit: RecordSentBatchUseCase { Result.success(Unit) } and ObserveHistoryUseCase { emptyFlow() }. Defaults are deliberately refused — a default turns a missing Koin binding into silently losing every batch.

risks.text: Disk + SQLite work inside resolveAndSend lengthens the send's perceived latency.
risks.mitigation: A few hundred KB on Dispatchers.IO inside an already multi-second operation. Documented single-line escape hatch (detached viewModelScope.launch) if ever measured as felt; not taken now because it makes SC-16 racy against the toast.

risks.text: Growing MirrorUiState with a list that changes on every DB emission adds reducer passes to a pixel-sensitive state machine.
risks.mitigation: Emissions happen once per send, not once per frame, and the BLOBs are a few KB decoded lazily by the row. This respects deviation 2 in presentation-feature-mirror/CLAUDE.md (pixels stay out of reduced state) because the thumbnail is bytes, not a decoded frame.

risks.text: Storing thumbnail bytes in the DB could be read as contradicting the closed 'paths, not BLOBs' decision.
risks.mitigation: Stated explicitly in this plan and in the entity's KDoc: frame.png and crop-N.png remain files on disk with paths in the DB exactly as decided; the BLOB is a separate derived few-KB thumbnail that exists only so a commonMain composable needs no file-reading seam.

risks.text: AC-34's badge can never be demonstrated end-to-end in F-8 because nothing ever writes In progress.
risks.mitigation: Unit-test the count-to-badge mapping (including the omit-at-zero branch) and seed one row manually in the DB during the demo. Never ship a fake transition to make a screenshot look right.

risks.text: Unbounded disk growth from retained frame/crop/hierarchy copies.
risks.mitigation: Closed, accepted ceiling (clarify decision). Marked with a `ponytail:` comment in BatchFileStore naming the upgrade path (age or count cap) rather than re-litigated.

risks.text: A failed DB insert is invisible to the user — one batch quietly missing from History.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: F-8 has no error surface and the alternative (failing the send) is explicitly ruled out. log.w carries the batch id. Cheap upgrade if it proves unacceptable: reuse the existing SendComplete snackbar path with a different summary.

functional.text: Provide a History tab listing every batch ever sent, grouped by time period, each row showing a thumbnail crop, title/summary, timestamp, and a status chip (e.g. Fixed, In progress).

On every successful AnnotationHandoff.publish (F-7), persist a new Batch record (frozen frame copy, per-annotation crop copies, hierarchy dump, prompt, sessionId, sentAtMs, device info) to the local Room database with initial status Sent.

Copy the frozen frame PNG and each per-annotation crop PNG from the handoff slot into app-owned storage at persist time, because F-7 prunes every handoff-slot image directory except the latest after each publish and a bare path reference would go stale.
Render History rows grouped under Today / Yesterday / Older headers, based on the batch's local calendar day relative to now, newest batch first within each group.
Compute each row's 44x44 thumbnail by running the existing crop() algorithm (pad=18, bw=bh=40) against the union bounding box of all of the batch's annotation rects.

Render each row's title as the batch's first annotation's comment text (ellipsised, single line) and its meta line as '<n> notes . <HH:mm sent time> . #<last 4 hex chars of batch id>'. CORRECTION OF RECORD: implemented as (id.hashCode() and 0xFFFF).toString(16).padStart(4, '0') — mintSessionId returns '<deviceId>-f<frameId>-<sentAtMs>' in decimal, so the literal wording is not satisfiable.

Render a status chip with a tone dot per BatchStatus value (Sent, In progress, Fixed, Verified, Follow-up sent), matching the design's tone mapping; Sent shares Verified's neutral tone since the prototype defines no distinct tone for it.
Show a Verify button only on rows with status Fixed; clicking it invokes a caller-supplied callback (no-op by default). The diff/verify logic itself is out of scope (F-9).

Expose a BatchRepository.updateStatus(batchId, BatchStatus) API for a future consumer (F-9) to drive In progress / Fixed / Verified / Follow-up sent transitions; F-8 itself never calls it beyond the initial Sent write.
Show History as the third segment of RectifyWindow's existing inspector tab strip, with a badge equal to the count of batches currently in In progress status (hidden when zero).
Show a footer line 'claude . session <sessionId>' sourced from the most recently persisted batch's sessionId; project path is omitted because AnnotationEnvelope carries no such field.
Keep all persisted batches visible indefinitely; no delete or retention UI ships in this spec.

nonFunctional.text: All mirror stream data, screenshots, hierarchy dumps, and payloads stay local to the machine; no network egress beyond localhost MCP communication.
History and batch metadata persist locally and survive app restarts.
The History list renders via a lazily-virtualized list (Compose LazyColumn) so UI render cost stays independent of total persisted batch count.
Copying frame and crop PNGs to durable per-batch storage at publish time runs off the UI thread, consistent with AnnotationHandoff's existing suspend contract.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given batches have been sent previously, when the History tab is opened, then batches are grouped by time period, each showing thumbnail, summary, timestamp, and status chip.
Given History contains at least one batch, when the app is quit and relaunched, then all batches, their status chips, stored frozen frames, and per-annotation records are still present and openable.
Given the History tab badge, when zero batches have status In progress, then no badge is shown on the tab; when N batches are In progress, the badge shows N.

Given a batch has more than one annotation, when its History row thumbnail is generated, then the crop is computed from the union bounding box of all of the batch's annotation rects, not just the first.
Given a batch's status, when its History row renders, then the Verify button is shown only for status Fixed and is absent for every other status.
Given at least one batch has been persisted, when the History list footer renders, then it shows 'claude . session <id>' sourced from the most recently persisted batch's sessionId.

Given F-7 prunes the handoff slot's image files after each publish, when a batch is persisted, then its frame and crop images have already been copied into app-owned storage so they remain available after subsequent sends and app restarts.

architecture.approach: One persistence vertical (entity + child entity + DAO + datasource + repository + mapper + two use cases) hung off the existing mirror surface, with one new side effect inside MirrorViewModel.resolveAndSend() and one new field on MirrorUiState. Write-after-success in its own failure domain; read through a bare Flow collected in the container init; render with LazyColumn over shipped design-system components; two edits in RectifyWindow.kt.
architecture.rationale: Persist-after-success was chosen over persist-before-publish (would show a lying 'Sent' row for a batch the agent never received, contradicting FR-26), over sharing publish's runCatching (a full disk could reduce SendPhase.Failed for a send that actually succeeded — the one outcome explicitly ruled out), and over a detached fire-and-forget launch (makes SC-16's row racy against the toast and escapes the test harness's advanceUntilIdle discipline) — for one extra .onFailure line. The brainstorm's key realisation holds: assembleEnvelope already returns (envelope, images) as in-memory values and held.bytes/held.bitmap are locals, so F-8 never reads anything back from ~/.rectify/handoff and FR-27/AC-38 are satisfied by construction, not by racing the pruner. A normalised child table beats a JSON blob because the blob would embed AnnotationEnvelope (documented as wire-breaking) in durable storage, store knowingly dead cropPaths, and drag kotlinx-serialization into presentation-feature-mirror; the child table costs ~30 lines and makes F-9's per-annotation 'resolved' flag a column add. A thumbnail BLOB beats thumb.png + path because a commonMain composable cannot read a file, so a path would require a whole new expect/actual image-loading seam for a single plate — and the BLOB makes 'the row survives manual file deletion' structural rather than defensive. BatchFileStore as a fun-interface Koin seam matches two existing precedents (CropEncoder, HandoffSourcesProvider), avoids adding okio/kotlinx-io for three file writes, and is the only option that lets SC-18 be unit-tested without a real disk.

alternativesConsidered.title: Persist before publish
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Shows status Sent for a batch the agent never received; contradicts FR-26/AC-38 and needs compensating deletion on publish failure — more code to be less correct.

alternativesConsidered.title: Persist inside publish's runCatching
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: A Room/IO failure would reduce SendPhase.Failed and tell the user a successful send failed. One saved line for an expensive class of false-negative bug.

alternativesConsidered.title: Detached viewModelScope.launch after publish
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Removes latency nobody has measured while making SC-16's row arrival racy against the toast and escaping advanceUntilIdle. Kept as a documented one-line escape hatch.

alternativesConsidered.title: Persist in the data layer by observing handoff.latest()
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: latest() reads the slot that is being pruned — exactly the staleness F-8 exists to avoid — and needs polling plus duplicate detection. AS-1 says one call-site hook suffices.

alternativesConsidered.title: Single annotationsJson TEXT column
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Embeds the wire-breaking AnnotationEnvelope in storage, persists dead handoff cropPaths, and adds a serialization dependency edge to presentation-feature-mirror.

alternativesConsidered.title: thumb.png on disk + path column
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Requires a new expect/actual image-file-reading seam whose only consumer is one 56dp plate, and reintroduces the missing-file failure mode the BLOB deletes.

alternativesConsidered.title: Store the full frame and crop at render time (as the HTML prototype does)
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Loads hundreds of KB per visible row, fighting NFR-13 for no benefit.

alternativesConsidered.title: New :presentation-feature-history Gradle module
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: MirrorHost's KDoc states there is exactly one call site; a second module would force a second koinViewModel() and a second ViewModel for a side-panel slot.

alternativesConsidered.title: Reuse core/payload/CropWindow.kt#cropWindow for the thumbnail
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Verified on disk: it uses designPad=14f into an 84×72 cell and returns a render window, not PNG bytes. FR-29 wants pad=18 into a 40×40 box and the result must be encoded once at persist time.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add an UpdateBatchStatusUseCase in F-8
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: FR-33 specifies a repository API; a use case with zero callers is scaffolding F-9 can add in one file when it has one.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add okio or kotlinx-io for the file writes
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: A new filesystem dependency for three file writes fails the reuse ladder; java.io in a desktopMain source set is the shipped precedent.

alternativesConsidered.title: Bump to @Database(version = 2) with MIGRATION_1_2
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Writes migration code no database can ever execute — nothing has ever injected AppDatabase and the relocation makes a pre-existing file impossible by construction.

errorStates.behavior: No persisted batches: MirrorHistoryTab early-returns an empty state copying MirrorNotesTab's shape, with mirror_history_empty. The footer is hidden when there is no batch (AC-37 is conditioned on 'at least one batch persisted').

No spinner. MirrorUiState.history defaults to emptyList() and the first Flow emission replaces it, typically within a frame of the panel opening; a transient empty state is indistinguishable from the genuine empty state and needs no extra UI.
DB read failure: HistoryRepositoryImpl.observe() is guarded with .catch { log.w(it); emit(emptyList()) }, so the tab degrades to the empty state and the mirror surface never crashes.

DB write failure (SQLiteException, disk full, locked file): mapped to Failure.Technical.Database by resultLauncher, returned as Result.failure, consumed in resolveAndSend with .onFailure { log.w } only. SendPhase is untouched, no side effect is posted, the send still reports success. One batch is silently missing from History — the accepted trade.

File write failure (SC-18): BatchFileStore returns null instead of throwing; the row is still inserted with dirPath/framePath/hierarchyPath = null and its thumbPng intact, so it renders completely. Only F-9's future diff needs the frame, and it existence-checks at use time.
Crop/thumbnail encoder returned null (Android/iOS stand-in, or any AWT failure): thumbPng is null and HistoryRow draws its bare plate. No separate placeholder asset exists or is needed.

Stored image path whose file the user deleted by hand: the row renders unchanged, because rendering reads only DB columns (thumbnail BLOB included) and performs zero filesystem reads. This is structural, not defensive.

Batch with zero annotations: unblocked by canSend today, but unionRect returns null, the thumbnail encode is skipped, thumbPng is null, the title falls back to neutral localised copy and the meta line reads '0 notes'. Nothing crashes.

DB open failure on first launch (unwritable ~/.rectify, corrupt file): Room builds lazily and opens on first query, so the failure surfaces inside the guarded observe() Flow (empty tab + log.w) or inside resultLauncher on the first write (logged), never as a Koin graph construction crash. DatabaseBuilder.desktop mkdirs() the directory first so the common case cannot fail.
Same-millisecond id collision: @Insert(onConflict = REPLACE) overwrites the parent row and its cascaded children rather than throwing.

logs: log.w on a failed recordSentBatch, including the batch id and the Failure type — the only trace of a silently missing row.
log.w inside HistoryRepositoryImpl.observe()'s .catch before emitting emptyList().
log.w inside FileSystemBatchFileStore's runCatching when a file write fails (path + reason), before returning null.
log.i one-liner in the MirrorIntent.VerifyBatch stub naming the batch id — the handler body F-9 replaces.
log.d (debug only) of the resolved database path on first build, so a support question about 'where is my data' is one log line.

accessibility.requirement: The thumbnail plate carries a contentDescription from mirror_history_thumbnail_description (localised, batch-title interpolated); a null thumbnail contributes no empty-string announcement.
Status is never colour-only: StatusPill always renders its text label alongside the tone dot, so the five statuses are distinguishable without colour perception.

The Verify button uses AppButtonSize.ListAction's shipped hit target and is reachable by keyboard focus traversal within the LazyColumn; it is omitted (not hidden-but-focusable) on non-Fixed rows so focus order matches what is visible.
Group headers use Theme.typography.overline with Theme.color.ink3 and act as list section labels; they are plain text items in the LazyColumn so screen-reader traversal hits them in order.
The History tab is reachable without a pointer via the already-shipped Cmd+3 shortcut (shortcutToTab), and the panel's existing focus handling is unchanged.
Title and meta are ellipsised, never truncated mid-glyph, and the full comment remains the semantic text of the row so assistive tech can read beyond the visual clip.
No new animation is introduced; any scroll/hover affordance resolves through Theme.motion so reducedMotion is honoured centrally.

performanceBudget.target: <= 8 KB per row (<=128px longest edge, PNG). Enforced by cropAndScale's maxEdgePx before encoding.
<= 150 ms for a 3-annotation batch (thumbnail encode + ~1 MB of file writes + one transaction), inside an already multi-second operation; all of it off the UI thread (NFR-14).
< 100 ms per emission on desktop, with queries on Dispatchers.IO via setQueryCoroutineContext.
<= 10 MB of thumbnail bytes in MirrorUiState.
Independent of total batch count (NFR-13) — LazyColumn composes only visible rows; the footer sits outside the scroll (design's flex:none).
One state emission per send (not per frame); no polling, no midnight timer.
Unbounded by design (accepted ceiling); ~0.5-2 MB per batch of frame + crops + hierarchy. Recorded in a `ponytail:` comment in BatchFileStore with the age/count-cap upgrade path.

i18n.notes: Only values/strings.xml (English) exists in this repo; no other locale ships yet. Keys follow <feature>_<element>. PLAN-AS-2: the repo has zero pluralStringResource usages and zero <plurals> resources, so the note count ships as two plain keys selected by a pure function — never a hand-concatenated 's'. No AAPT-style apostrophe escapes (regression fixed in dae0893). The footer string carries the separator and the 'claude' literal with the session id interpolated; the meta string interpolates note count, time and short id. Every piece of copy in MirrorHistoryTab resolves through stringResource — the contract types carry no labels, matching the module's existing convention.

dataHandling: NFR-4: nothing leaves the machine. No HTTP client exists in the dependency graph of any module F-8 touches, and none is added; storage is the local filesystem plus a local SQLite file.
All app-owned data consolidates under ~/.rectify (rectify.db + history/ + the existing handoff/), so a user who wants to erase Rectify's data deletes one directory.
Hierarchy XML can be hundreds of KB and may contain on-screen text: it is written as a file inside the batch directory, never into a list-query column, and never logged.
Annotation comments and prompts are persisted in TEXT columns and never emitted to logs; log lines carry batch ids only.
Batch directory names are sanitised with [^A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by '_' so a device id can never escape the history root via path traversal.
permissions: Desktop filesystem access to the user's home directory only — already exercised by F-7's handoff slot; no new OS permission, no new entitlement, no network permission.
privacy: No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporting carries annotation text, prompts, screenshots or hierarchy dumps.
No retention policy ships (FR-36): data persists until the user deletes ~/.rectify/history. This is a deliberate, recorded ceiling; a future retention spec owns the delete affordance.
File permissions are whatever java.io creates under the user's home (owner-readable); no attempt is made to broaden them.

featureFlags: None. The tab segment already exists and currently renders nothing (`else -> Unit`); filling it is additive and desktop-only, so a flag would guard a hole rather than a risk.
migrations: No Room Migration. @Database(version = 1) stands because the desktop file relocates from ~/rectify.db to ~/.rectify/rectify.db in the same change and neither path exists on any machine (verified on disk; AppDatabase is a lazy Koin single nothing has ever injected). The relocation and the stay-at-v1 ship together or not at all.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Crop cell fitted to a constant 84dp but drawn in weight(1f), clipping the outline at narrow panel widths; cropWindow's KDoc about the pad was inaccurate.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: Repeating the same mistake in the thumbnail: sizing the crop against a constant while the plate is laid out by the parent. The thumbnail plate is HistoryRow's fixed 56dp (not a weighted cell), and thumbnailRect scales its pad by frameWidth/designWidth exactly like cropWindow does.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Compute thumbnailRect purely from the frame size and the union rect, encode once at persist time, and let the plate scale the decoded bitmap with ContentScale — no composable-side arithmetic (the constraint TAC-4 already imposed).

knownRisksFromQA.description: Tautological test asserting a literal against itself (assertEquals(1, PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION)) — would pass under any edit.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The same shape creeping into HistoryFormattingTest, e.g. asserting the status-to-tone map by restating the map, or asserting shortBatchId against hashCode recomputed in the test.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Assert behaviour against hand-computed literals: a fixed id string to a fixed 4-char expected value, three concrete rects to one concrete union, three fixed epochs across a day boundary to the expected group split.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Test name and comment claimed a structural property the body never asserted (Empty to empty, twice).
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: A groupHistory test named for ordering that only checks group names, or an SC-18 test named for the row surviving that only checks the store returned null.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Every new test's assertions must name-match its title; the SC-18 test asserts the datasource received an insert with null paths AND a non-null thumbnail, not merely that nothing threw.

knownRisksFromQA.description: core/payload file names do not partition their contents — one label function in PayloadLabels.kt while two live in PayloadEstimate.kt; PayloadGate.kt holds three unrelated predicates.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: core/history/ repeating it by scattering grouping, formatting and geometry across ad-hoc files, or by becoming a junk drawer.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Exactly two files with crisp boundaries: HistoryFormatting.kt (pure text/time/id/tone/geometry decisions) and ThumbnailBitmap.kt (the one non-pure bitmap helper). Anything that is neither goes in a third, named file — never appended to these.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Kotlin/Native release linker OOMs under ~4 parallel linkReleaseFramework tasks against a 4 GiB daemon heap.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The cross-target gate (step 13) hanging or dying with 'Java heap space' — pre-existing, affects every cross-target build in this repo, not caused by F-8.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Run the cross-target gate with --max-workers=1, as every prior spec did. Do not debug it as an F-8 failure; the real fix (kotlin.native.linkerThreads or a bigger daemon heap) is its own task.

knownRisksFromQA.description: HierarchyRow's `matched` is exactly `tag != null` at every call site yet defaults false, dimming the tree for forgetful consumers — a defaulted parameter that silently degrades behaviour.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The same trap in the new code: a defaulted MirrorViewModel use-case parameter would turn a missing Koin binding into silently losing every batch.
